original.target_description: Study 1b: MTurk participants viewed high- versus low-elevation scenery; repeated-measures ANOVA of likelihood of purchasing four new products, elevation as the between-participants factor; main effect of elevation.

n.sample_role: Participants in Study 1b repeated-measures purchase-likelihood analysis; 96 low elevation and 107 high elevation, as printed in Table 2.
n.exclusions: No exclusions stated in Study 1b methods/results. Table 2 identifies the study sample; methods report 203 recruited, and target ANOVA F(1, 201) is consistent with all 203 participants.
n.location: Published p.235 (PDF p.6), Table 2, Study 1b header; p.236 (PDF p.7), Study 1b Method and Results.
n.quote: Study 1b (Likelihood of Purchasing New Products; N ¼ 203, 41% Male, Mage ¼ 36.4 Years, MTurk)

es.location: Published p.236 (PDF p.7), Study 1b Results, main effect of elevation.

p.location: Published p.236 (PDF p.7), Study 1b Results, same main effect of elevation as partial eta-squared.

notes: Original-only blind validation. Supplied source is the published Journal of Marketing Research article, 2019, 56(2), 230–244, title and DOI matched in canonical text. Visually inspected rendered PDF pages 6 and 7 (published pp.235–236). Canonical-text quotes preserve extraction glyphs: ¼ represents the rendered equals sign, and Z2 represents rendered eta-squared (η²); the printed result is partial η² = .029. Table 2 rounds the same overall p to .02; the Results paragraph supplies .016, retained here with its matching effect size. No statistic conversion. Perceived control is not the Study 1b outcome; the located target is its overall new-product purchase-likelihood main effect. Unassigned replication and narrative-success fields are placeholders only.
